name: Civil libertarianism
summary: Civil libertarianism defends individual rights and freedoms, above all free speech, privacy, due process, equal protection and religious freedom, against the state, and against majority or social pressure. It holds that coercion is justified only to prevent harm to others and that unpopular people and speech must be protected because those rights protect everyone. It takes no stand on economic policy.
scope: The mainstream liberal and Millian civil-liberties tradition as practised by the ACLU and similar groups, drawn from Mill's On Liberty and the ACLU's mission and cases. It excludes economic libertarianism, which Wikipedia says civil libertarianism does not require.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Civil libertarianism is a stance on liberties, not on health financing; adherents are split along their separate economic views.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wikipedia notes civil libertarianism does not address economic policy, so adherents hold varied views on wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The ideology is silent on economic allocation; a civil libertarian may or may not be an economic libertarian.

public-ownership.rationale: Economic ownership is outside the ideology's scope, so adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax rates are not a civil-liberties question; adherents follow their separate economic leanings.

unions-good.rationale: The ACLU defends labor speech and assembly rights but takes no stance on whether unions benefit society.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are not the focus of civil libertarianism, which centres on speech, privacy and due process; adherents differ.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporate regulation is explicitly an area the ideology leaves open, per Wikipedia.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The ACLU's post-9/11 work and its opposition to the Patriot Act reject trading privacy for security, and Carpenter v. US required a warrant for location data.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Mill's rule that society may coerce only to prevent harm to others, and that a person is sovereign over his own body, supports adult drug freedom.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Civil libertarians oppose bans on hate speech and obscenity; the ACLU defended Nazis and the Klan because protection matters most for repugnant messages.

strong-leader.rationale: Mill's warning that unchecked power, even popular, oppresses individuals makes bypassing institutional checks unacceptable.

state-harmful.rationale: Civil libertarians want state power limited and checked, but they rely on courts and constitutions rather than seeking to abolish the state.

limit-guns.rationale: The ACLU opposes a national gun registry yet accepts some gun regulation, and other civil libertarians defend gun rights, so adherents are split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: The ACLU's focus on policing abuses, prisoners' rights and post-9/11 security overreach leads adherents to resist expanding coercive powers.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

rehabilitation.rationale: The ACLU supports prisoners' rights and decarceration, favouring reform over pure punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: The ideology neither endorses nor opposes the social value of family forms; it only rejects legal imposition of them.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The ACLU argued Lawrence v. Texas and US v. Windsor and supports same-sex marriage as an equal-protection and privacy right.

abortion-legal.rationale: The ACLU defends legal abortion as a privacy right (s3), but some libertarian-leaning civil libertarians differ, so the answer is contested.

more-religion-public.rationale: The ACLU supports separation of church and state and opposes government preference for religion or official school prayer.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The ACLU lists equality for people of color among its focus areas, though means such as preferences are contested.

gradual-change.rationale: Civil libertarians work through courts and law but have no doctrine on pace of social change.

free-trade.rationale: Economic policy is expressly outside civil libertarianism per Wikipedia.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a civil-liberties question; adherents are split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Open dissent and competing opinion are central to Mill's case, and the ACLU defends unpopular political speech.

democracy-best.rationale: Mill and the ACLU favour democratic government but hold it must be limited by individual rights, since majorities can tyrannise.

natural-rulers.rationale: The ideology rests on equal rights and Mill's rejection of claimed infallibility, so inherent fitness to rule is rejected.

political-violence-never.rationale: Civil libertarians oppose state violence but have no unified pacifist doctrine.

separate-church-state.rationale: The ACLU supports separation of church and state and opposes official prayer in public schools.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Basing law on scripture imposes religious doctrine and conflicts with the ACLU's church-state separation.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The ACLU's equal-protection work for all groups, including defending Japanese Americans against internment, opposes ethnic definitions of the nation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The ideology demands equal rights, not any distribution of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land authority is not a core civil-liberties matter; the ACLU's equality work does not settle it either way.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Wikipedia states civil libertarians prioritise individual rights and freedoms over any authority, including the state.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: A verdict on industrial civilization is not part of the civil-liberties tradition; adherents are split.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The ACLU's work on digital-age privacy, including Carpenter v. US, supports private communication shielded from state access.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial power over a class means stripping rights from an unpopular group, which the ACLU opposes because such rights can later be used against everyone.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a civil-liberties position; adherents differ by economic outlook.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill states that society may coerce an individual only to prevent harm to others, and that his own good is not sufficient warrant.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Wikipedia says the movement puts individual rights above authority, though the ACLU also litigates for groups' equal treatment.

positive-liberty.rationale: The ideology emphasises freedom from state interference but the ACLU also pursues equality; split.

total-state.rationale: A state directing every area of life denies Mill's individual sovereignty over his own mind and body.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by personal oaths contradicts constitutional, rights-bound government that the ACLU seeks to realise.

bound-labor.rationale: Legally tying people to land and lord denies individual liberty and equal rights before the law.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mill defends open debate as a path toward truth, which sits uneasily with the view that all knowledge is power-laden.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not a civil-liberties question; church-state concerns cut against religious vouchers.

economic-freedom.rationale: Civil libertarianism takes no position on economic liberty (s4), and adherents differ on whether political freedom depends on it.

national-self-determination.rationale: Statehood for nations is not a question civil libertarianism answers; adherents vary.

force-without-un.rationale: Use of force abroad is a foreign-policy matter beyond the ideology, with adherents wary of war powers but split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mill defends free debate but the ACLU defends religious belief too, so no stance on faith as a guide.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditions are not a core question.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts of states are a foreign-policy question with no civil-libertarian position.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The ACLU lists equality for women among its focus areas, so legally distinct roles are rejected.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The ACLU took part in Brown v. Board of Education against legal segregation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Wikipedia and Mill both object to pressure to conform; forced cultural abandonment is such pressure.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim; the ACLU defends immigrants but takes no stance on this empirical assertion.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Compelled or pressured reproduction decisions violate the bodily privacy the ACLU defends.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The ACLU opposes torture and defends prisoners' rights, supporting legal accountability for abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wikipedia says civil libertarians need not hold libertarian economic views, so minimal-state doctrine is not shared.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Social and legal pressure on private choices is the conformity Mill condemns and the ACLU opposes under equal protection.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The ACLU's mission is equal protection and constitutional rights for all, including the unpopular.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal law is attractive but religious freedom pulls the other way; adherents split.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The ACLU defends religious freedom, which includes freedom to change religion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The ACLU opposes official prayer and government preference for religion in public schools.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is economic and, per Wikipedia, outside civil libertarianism.

population-transfer.rationale: The ACLU opposed Japanese American internment, a forced removal of a minority seen as hostile.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: A philosophy-of-history claim; Mill values open debate but this statement is about struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The ACLU defends the speech of Nazis and Klansmen, and Mill treats silencing as presuming infallibility, so banning parties is rejected.

separated-powers.rationale: Mill's concern about unchecked power and the ACLU's reliance on constitutional checks favour dividing power.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The ACLU's early focus was on speech and assembly in the labor movement, so legal limits on picketing are viewed with suspicion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selecting offices by lottery is an electoral-design question with no civil-libertarian position.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The ACLU formed in response to the Palmer Raids' arrests without warrants and has opposed internment and post-9/11 overreach.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mill argues all silencing of discussion assumes infallibility, and speakers' and listeners' rights bar state control of information.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars conflicts with church-state separation and equal religious freedom.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Civil libertarians oppose bans on obscenity, and Mill rejects suppressing opinions for their supposed harmfulness.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances and troop deployments are foreign policy, not civil liberties.

people-in-arms.rationale: The ACLU's mixed gun stance leaves adherents split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: A sociological generalisation about graduates that civil libertarianism does not make.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not a civil-liberties doctrine; adherents protect cultural practice as individual liberty only.

death-penalty.rationale: The ACLU opposes capital punishment, regarded as a violation of rights and due process.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The ACLU's Scopes case and church-state stance oppose religious doctrine in public-school science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Wikipedia states civil libertarians oppose legal bans on obscenity.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious liberty favours exemptions, equal law disfavours them; adherents split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill warns that social pressure to conform can oppress more than law and 'enslave the soul', and treats individuality as essential.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: How a head of state is chosen is not a civil-liberties question.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions in peace deals are foreign policy beyond the ideology.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist historical classification the ideology does not weigh in on.

collective-defense.rationale: Treaty alliance obligations are foreign policy, not civil liberties.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State control of clergy violates the religious freedom the ACLU defends.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not a civil-liberties issue.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is a territorial question the ideology does not address; adherents split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements are not a civil-liberties issue.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Official sacralisation of a ruler conflicts with Mill's rejection of claimed infallibility and church-state separation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The ACLU's mission is realising constitutional limits and due process for everyone, including against the state.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-regime theory is not part of civil-libertarian doctrine, which stresses limits rather than regime form.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing a person's own religious choice contradicts Mill's harm principle and the ACLU's religious freedom.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelled dress for adults harms no one else, so Mill's principle forbids it.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority self-government in culture is not specifically addressed; adherents split between group and individual-rights views.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Mill's tyranny-of-the-majority argument and the ACLU's defence of rights even when unpopular require courts that can constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Mandated quotas are contested among adherents; equal treatment pulls both ways.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mill himself allowed despotism over 'backward' peoples, but modern adherents reject rule without consent on equal-rights grounds.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The ACLU supports equality measures but colour-blind arguments also appeal; split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A prediction about capitalism's crises that civil libertarianism does not make.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The ACLU backs anti-discrimination equality, though libertarian-leaning civil libertarians value freedom of association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The ACLU's stated purpose is to realise the promise of the Constitution and its rights for all.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Unlimited legislative supremacy conflicts with entrenched protections against majorities.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A duty of the privileged is a conservative ethic that civil libertarianism neither endorses nor rejects.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal protection and immigrant-rights advocacy oppose citizen-class distinctions in public office.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Reserving leadership by descent conflicts with equal political rights.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The ACLU opposes fascist state power but defends fascists' speech; split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument policy is a heritage question; the ideology protects speech but does not mandate preservation.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political army above civilian law contradicts constitutional rights protection.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service selection by exam is administrative design, not a civil-liberties issue.

corporate-influence.rationale: The ACLU opposes campaign-finance limits that infringe speech while supporting public financing; split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Financial birth incentives are a population-policy question; adherents accept voluntary incentives but the sources are silent.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is labor organisation outside civil libertarianism.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The ACLU defends unpopular minorities, and rights taken from them can be used against everyone.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Whether marriage should confer legal benefits is a policy matter the sources do not settle; adherents split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarchist organising style is not a civil-liberties position, though freedom of association protects it.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Priority between domestic and international law is not settled; adherents use both to protect rights.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion conflicts with equal religious freedom and equal protection.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A historical judgement on capitalism that civil libertarianism does not make.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Whether women's equality requires economic transformation is a theory dispute; the ACLU pursues legal equality without taking a side.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small cooperative communities are an economic-social model; civil libertarians accept voluntary ones but take no side.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Weighing historical against current claims is a territorial dispute the ideology does not decide.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The claim is factually rejected by civil libertarians, who nonetheless defend the right to voice it, as with the ACLU in the Skokie case.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The ACLU litigated Lawrence v. Texas, which struck down criminal sodomy laws on privacy grounds.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mill treats silencing dissent as assuming infallibility and the ACLU defends unpopular political groups.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Civil libertarianism defends offensive speech and the ACLU opposes state preference for any religion.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious duty of armed resistance is outside civil libertarianism, which defends belief but not violence.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Declaring rulers illegitimate by religious law and removing them by force contradicts church-state separation and lawful rights protection.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct participation in workplaces and communities is a democratic-design question, not settled by civil libertarianism.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The ACLU lists several equality fields but takes no theory position.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The ACLU lists LGBTQ equality among its focus areas.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Whether left and right are outdated is a framing question; the ideology is cross-partisan but makes no claim.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The ACLU defends religious equality and holds that rights for unpopular groups protect everyone.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Constitutional government by the consent of the people and church-state separation reject divinely sourced authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Bans on religious dress restrict expression and conscience, though state-actor officials are a closer question.

property-franchise.rationale: Limiting the vote by wealth violates the equal rights before the law the ACLU defends.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Civil libertarians hold press and assembly freedoms meaningful as legal protections against the state, so this critique is rejected.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Due process and the rule of law, central to the ACLU's constitutional mission, require known laws applied by courts.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is a democratic-design question; adherents like open participation but sources are silent.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Such a law restricts a private choice in conflict with religious freedom and privacy.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly selected assemblies are a democratic-design question not settled by civil libertarianism.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious doctrine is the believers' own affair; civil libertarians defend whichever stance they take.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The ACLU lists LGBTQ equality as a focus area, supporting equal treatment in service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State promotion of any stance on religion violates the ACLU's neutrality principle.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The ACLU supports reform and decarceration but not abolition.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a procedural innovation with no civil-libertarian position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Internal religious governance is protected as religious freedom; adherents differ.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Mill's harm principle permits coercion to prevent harm to others, which accepts defensive force but treats initiating force against others as unjustified.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Civil libertarians prioritise rights over state goals; the ACLU opposes trading liberties for national objectives, as with security.

racial-franchise.rationale: The ACLU's equal-protection mission, including Brown v. Board, rules out limiting votes or offices by race.

abolish-ip.rationale: Civil libertarianism takes no stand on property; Mill and the ACLU defend speech, so adherents are divided on abolishing patents and copyrights.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition itself is not a civil-liberties question, though the ACLU opposes laws punishing denial, so adherents are split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The ACLU defends church-state separation, which counts against framing politics as a struggle between good and evil.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Equal protection is a core civil-liberties principle, and the ACLU's mission opposes laws favouring one group over another in economic life.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership is an economic matter on which civil libertarians are split.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative structure is not a civil-liberties question; adherents differ.

family-wage.rationale: Wage policy is economic and outside civil libertarianism.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Economic and regulatory question outside the civil-liberties focus; adherents split.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Research funding is outside the civil-liberties focus; adherents split.

online-anonymity.rationale: The ACLU has defended anonymous speech, and privacy and free expression are core civil liberties.

person-over-state.rationale: Mill's On Liberty holds that individuals may not be coerced for the community's benefit except to prevent harm to others.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Civil libertarianism is neutral on spiritual questions beyond protecting religious freedom.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural technology is outside civil libertarianism.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is outside civil libertarianism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Military policy is outside civil libertarianism; adherents are split.

free-public-college.rationale: Economic and education finance are outside civil libertarianism; adherents split.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Wikipedia notes civil libertarianism takes no stance on economic policy, so adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Foreign and defence policy is outside the ideology; adherents split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Civil libertarianism distrusts concentrated state power and defends the right to bear arms for many adherents, though the ACLU takes no firm line; adherents are mixed so a lean only.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The tradition is explicitly silent on economic policy, so adherents split along their separate economic views.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation is an economic and political-economy question outside civil libertarianism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Mill's emphasis on individuality and experiments in living cuts against a fixed, non-redesignable human nature, though rights are grounded in dignity; adherents are mixed.

public-service-media.rationale: Civil libertarians value press freedom and fear government control of media; the ACLU defends speech and press freedom but adherents split on public funding.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Civil libertarianism concerns the liberties of belief, not which belief is true; adherents hold every view on the question.

farm-price-support.rationale: An economic question; Wikipedia notes civil libertarianism does not require any particular economic position, so adherents are split.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: A foreign-policy and defence question outside civil liberties; adherents divide along their separate views.

voter-id.rationale: The ACLU opposes strict voter-ID and proof-of-citizenship rules as burdens on the right to vote and equal protection.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Religious freedom and equal protection are core civil-liberties commitments, which rule out giving one interpretation of a religion legal precedence.

premarital-sex.rationale: Mill's harm principle and the privacy tradition treat consensual private conduct as outside state or social coercion.

negative-income-tax.rationale: A matter of welfare design that the tradition leaves to adherents' separate economic views.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal protection and equal civil rights regardless of sex are central to the ACLU's mission.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Adherents are split between backing equal-treatment enforcement and distrusting new state bodies; the tradition does not address it.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Civil libertarianism takes no stand on economics, and adherents split on property origins along their separate economic views.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Adherents are split between valuing due process and fear of unaccountable supranational power; the sources read do not settle it.

national-church-status.rationale: Religious freedom and equal treatment of beliefs lead civil libertarians, such as the ACLU, to oppose official preference for one religion.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The ACLU defends due process and the right to trial for the despised, and killing suspects without trial negates it.

close-ties-china.rationale: The tradition takes no stand on great-power alignment; adherents are split, though some object to China's record on rights.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Civil libertarianism takes no stand on economics, and Wikipedia says it does not require economic libertarianism; adherents split on resource ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: Mill holds that over his own body and mind the individual is sovereign, and the ACLU defends bodily autonomy and privacy, though it does not frame rights as property in oneself.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy lies outside its remit; adherents are split along their separate economic views.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare design is not a civil-liberties question, and adherents divide on it.

no-business-privileges.rationale: An economic question the tradition leaves open; adherents are split.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: It protects religious freedom and opposes establishment, but also protects the right of religious groups to organise politically, so it is split.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Equal protection and individual liberty mean a spouse may not be held in a marriage against their will.

national-resource-control.rationale: Economic ownership is outside its concern; adherents split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Economic policy is outside civil libertarianism, so adherents are split along their separate economic views.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The ACLU fights racial discrimination, but the question of whether racism is still the main obstacle is an empirical one on which adherents differ.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Mill's harm principle supports resisting unjust laws, and the ACLU backs civil disobedience cases, but the natural-law claim is not part of the doctrine and adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: An economic question the doctrine does not address; adherents hold varied views.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: One-party rule is incompatible with the free speech, association and due-process protections the ACLU and Mill defend, whatever the economic system.

police-more-powers.rationale: The ACLU's focus on policing abuses, prisoners' rights and post-9/11 security overreach leads adherents to resist expanding coercive powers. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: Government should need a warrant from a court before searching a person's private communications or location data.
missingStatements.rationale: The ACLU's digital-privacy work, including Carpenter v. United States, centres on warrant requirements for such data.

missingStatements.text: Speech that is offensive or unpopular should be legally protected unless it causes imminent harm.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill and the SEP both allow restriction only where harm is imminent and discussion impossible, and the ACLU defended Skokie.

missingStatements.text: People accused of a crime should have the right to a fair trial and legal counsel, even when they are widely despised.
missingStatements.rationale: Due process for the unpopular is a founding purpose of the ACLU, formed after warrantless Palmer Raids arrests.
missingStatements.declined: Fair trial for the accused is near-universally accepted, so not contested; equal-moral-worth covers it.

notes: Civil libertarians include left-liberal (ACLU) and libertarian-leaning strands; they diverge on guns, abortion, discrimination law and campaign finance. Many answers beyond liberties are low-confidence inferences because Wikipedia says the ideology is silent on economic policy.
